# Policymaker #411, iteration 0073

## Decision
I ordered one fix task: `reason-selftest-408-409` (benchmark role, medium effort, 45 min, 35 turns, from main, wake false).

## Why
- Review #408 of the change cases (#404) returned `verdict: revise`. Blocking finding 2: if you disable the expected-reason comparison at `benchmark/scripts/change_cases.py:118`, `--check` still exits 0.
- Review #409 of the precision plan (#405) returned `verdict: revise`. It had the same blocking finding at `benchmark/scripts/precision_plan.py:170`.
- All other spec checks, hash checks and probes passed. Evidence: `.session/history/sessions/408/f20d1c0e….md` and `.session/history/sessions/409/9bd8a2c9….md`.
- One task fixes both checkers. It uses the reviewed reason self-test pattern of `runner_contract.py` (#364, reviewed in #369).

## Expected gain and check
- Expected gain: both checkers detect when the reason comparison is removed. Then one re-review can accept them, and a script can pin both designs.
- Check in the next session: both `--check` commands exit 0 on main. The report also gives the new sha256 values and revert-probe exit codes that are not zero.

## Limits that stay visible
- Both reviewers were GPT family (codex), the same family as authors #404 and #405. A model-family limit stays recorded.
- Native evidence (#169) and the store record for Owner request #379 are not available yet. Benchmark readiness is not established. Product quality is not measured. Product implementation stays gated.

## What next
- After the fix merges, order one re-review. The re-review checks only finding 2 and the new hashes (prefer a Claude reviewer).
- After the re-review accepts, use a hash-gated pin script: change-cases under tasks, precision under baseline (max_turns >= 25).
- Then submit the corrected #403 method-acceptance draft as a `question` request.
- Do not repeat the #408/#409 spec checks.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
